commands.review_summary:
The branch gates bundled Google Gemini CLI runtime provider/backend registration behind `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_GOOGLE_GEMINI_CLI_HARNESS`, preserves setup-registry compatibility for auth/runtime routing, and updates Google provider docs/tests.

PR surface: Source +81, Tests +168, Docs +59. Total +308 across 14 files.

Reproducibility: yes. for the PR behavior: current main and `v2026.6.11` register the Gemini CLI backend/provider by default, while PR head omits both when the env flag is unset. The PR body also includes redacted terminal proof for unset-env, opt-in, and setup-compatibility paths.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] Manual review is needed because the blocker is maintainer policy for a shipped default-registration and auth-provider upgrade behavior, not a narrow mechanical repair.

target.title: feat(google): gate Gemini CLI runtime harness behind explicit opt-in
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a Google provider compatibility problem where the bundled Google plugin exposes the Gemini CLI harness through direct runtime plugin registration by default, even though the supported default Google model path should remain the API-backed `google` provider.

The affected workflow is Google provider setup/runtime selection. This PR keeps existing setup-registry `google-gemini-cli` backend compatibility available while requiring explicit operator opt-in for direct bundled runtime registration of the Gemini CLI provider/backend.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change makes the Google provider boundary explicit: `google` remains the API-backed Google AI Studio/Gemini provider, `google-vertex` remains the Vertex provider, and `google-gemini-cli` is treated as an optional local CLI harness.

The opt-in is controlled by `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_GOOGLE_GEMINI_CLI_HARNESS=1`. This applies only to direct bundled runtime plugin registration. The setup-registry default for `google-gemini-cli` remains available so existing setup-only backend resolution continues to work.

The PR also aligns manifest metadata, onboarding copy, provider contract copy, public Google provider docs, and docs navigation with that compatibility policy.

## User Impact

Users configuring the default Google provider continue to see the API-backed Google path instead of being directed toward Gemini CLI OAuth by default.

Existing `google-gemini-cli` setup/backend resolution remains available through the setup-registry compatibility path. Operators who want direct bundled runtime registration of the Gemini CLI provider/backend can set `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_GOOGLE_GEMINI_CLI_HARNESS=1`.

## Evidence

### Current-head proof summary

- Current PR head: `99a15731d5e6eba510b3f6f037e6af3c00431f46`
- Gemini CLI runtime opt-in is documented directly in `docs/providers/google.md`.
- CLI backend docs now call out the Gemini CLI env-gated registration exception.
- The Google provider runtime contract is aligned by enabling the Gemini CLI harness for the contract tests that intentionally require `google-gemini-cli`.
- Existing Gemini CLI OAuth auth profiles are preserved through setup-registry runtime compatibility.
- Direct `google` auth profiles keep precedence and do not silently fall through to Gemini CLI.

### Targeted regression tests

Command run:

    pnpm vitest run src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.test.ts extensions/google/index-harness-registration.test.ts

Result:

    Test Files  3 passed (3)
    Tests  33 passed (33)

Coverage:

- Existing `google-gemini-cli` auth profiles still route canonical `google/*` execution through the Gemini CLI runtime.
- Legacy Gemini CLI auth order migrates to canonical `google` provider execution with `google-gemini-cli` as runtime.
- Direct `google` auth profiles keep precedence.
- Default bundled runtime registration still omits Gemini CLI unless `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_GOOGLE_GEMINI_CLI_HARNESS=1` is set.

### Provider runtime contract tests

Command run:

    pnpm vitest run ./extensions/google/provider-runtime.contract.test.ts

Result:

    Test Files  1 passed (1)
    Tests  5 passed (5)

Coverage:

- Confirms the Google provider runtime contract still owns `google` forward-compatible model resolution.
- Confirms the contract path that intentionally requires `google-gemini-cli` runs with the Gemini CLI harness env enabled.
- Confirms Gemini CLI provider runtime behavior still owns forward-compatible model resolution, OAuth token parsing, auth-profile formatting, and usage snapshot fetching.

### Redacted real setup terminal proof

This proof was run against the current PR head and exercises the actual Google bundled plugin runtime registration path. It is not a Vitest-only assertion.

Redaction note: the command does not print OAuth tokens, API keys, credential file contents, user credential values, or provider secrets.

Proof scope:

- Default-disabled runtime registration path with `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_GOOGLE_GEMINI_CLI_HARNESS` unset
- Opt-in-enabled runtime registration path with `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_GOOGLE_GEMINI_CLI_HARNESS=1`
- Setup compatibility metadata and backend factory path with the env flag unset

Terminal output:

Result summary:

- Default-disabled path confirmed: with `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_GOOGLE_GEMINI_CLI_HARNESS` unset, the bundled runtime registers only `google` and registers no `google-gemini-cli` CLI backend.
- Opt-in-enabled path confirmed: with `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_GOOGLE_GEMINI_CLI_HARNESS=1`, the bundled runtime registers `google-gemini-cli` and its CLI backend.
- Setup compatibility confirmed: with the env flag unset, plugin metadata still exposes `google-gemini-cli`, the OAuth auth choice remains present, and the backend factory still resolves the `google-gemini-cli` CLI backend.
- Runtime-alias behavior confirmed by targeted regression tests at the same current head.
- Provider runtime contract alignment confirmed by contract tests at the same current head.
- Local proof helper files were untracked and not committed.
